titleStmt.title: Memorandum From Constantine Menges and Oliver North of the National Security Council Staff to the President’s Assistant for National Security Affairs (McFarlane)

div.head: 472. Memorandum From Constantine Menges and Oliver North of the National Security Council Staff to the President’s Assistant for National Security Affairs (McFarlane)

list.label: SUBJECT
list.item: Secretary Shultz’ visit to Venezuela, Brazil, and El Salvador

div.p: Attached at Tab I is a memo from you to the President concerning the proposal by Secretary Shultz that he lead the delegation to the inauguration of President-elect Lusinchi, and subsequently visit Brazil and El Salvador as had been planned in October. The memo from Shultz to the President is attached at Tab A.

Your memo endorses the proposal of Secretary Shultz. It also informs the President that there are two factions within the just-elected social democratic party of Venezuela—one led by the President-elect with a strong labor union base which is realistic about the communist threat in Central America, and the other led by former President Carlos Andres Perez, which has been naive in expecting positive results from coalitions with the communists in Central America.

We think it important that, between now and the visit of Secretary Shultz, we send one or two senior officials to meet with President-elect Lusinchi in Caracas, Venezuela for an exchange of views on the situation in Central America and our objectives. Yesterday, a leading member of the Venezuelan private sector and friend of the President-elect, urged that this be done in the course of a meeting on another subject with [less than one line not declassified] and Menges. The weeks before President-elect Lusinchi assumes the responsibilities of office is an ideal time to provide him and his key advisors with the factual information and background briefing materials which can prepare the way for constructive results when Secretary Shultz and his group arrive.

You had approved my travel with Secretary Shultz to Brazil and El Salvador in October, and I would like to request that you approve my travel with the Secretary on this trip to Venezuela, Brazil and El Salvador. As an observer at the various meetings with our Ambassadors, I believe such a trip would add to my effectiveness here at the NSC.
That you sign and forward the memo to the President, and that you approve my travel with the Secretary on this trip and suggest this to him.

note.p: Source: Reagan Library, Executive Secretariat, NSC Country File, Latin America/Central, Venezuela (11/02/1982–12/20/1983). Secret. Sent for action. A stamped notation at the top of the page reads: “SIGNED.”

In telegram 10564 from Caracas, December 5, the Embassy reported on Landau’s meeting with Lusinchi in the early hours of December 5 following the December 4 election, noting “the president-elect made it very clear that good relations with the United States will be a major priority of his administration.” The Embassy added: “In total I left this meeting more convinced than ever that Lusinchi will go to great lengths to prove his friendship for the United States and that he will be a practical leader who listens to advice but one who has some very strong convictions as specific vision of what Venezuelan-U.S. relations should be.” (Department of State, Central Foreign Policy File, Electronic Telegrams, D830715–0831)
No memorandum of conversation has been found.
McFarlane indicated his approval by writing his initials.
